 JUDGMENT

sentences.text: This appeal is preferred by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 03.11.2020 passed by XX Additional Small Causes Judge and XVIII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate and MACT, Bengaluru (SCCH-22) (for short 'the tribunal') in MVC.No.2205/2018.
This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequacy of compensation awarded by the tribunal.
Hence, the appellant seeks enhancement of compensation.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as under;
That on 25.02.2018 at about 7.45 p.m, the claimant was travelling in a Indica Car bearing registration No.KA-02-MA- 0589 from Huliyurdurga to Devasandra.

When the Car reached NC:
2024:KHC:14599 near Hittlapura forest, Huliyurdurga main road, Tumakuru District at that time the Indica Car driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, unmindfully, without following the rules and regulations lost control over the vehicle and dashed to the road side bridge.
Due to injuries suffered in the accident, the claimant filed a claim petition seeking compensation against the respondents.
3.1. On service of notice, respondent No.1 was placed ex-parte.

Respondent No.2-Insurance Company filed statement of objections, denied the claim of the claimant including age, avocation,
income and the negligence attributed against the driver of the Car.
It is also pleaded that the claimant has quarreled with the owner of the offending vehicle and the police authority and filed the false and frivolous case only to make unlawful gain.
Accordingly, sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
3.2. On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.

In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the claimants got examined himself as PW.1 and Doctor as PW.3 and another one as PW.2 and got marked Sri Nagaraja D P vs Sri Kiran R on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164185336/
2 documents as Exs.P1 to P20.

sentences.text: On the other hand, respondents did not adduce their evidence either orally or documentary.

3.4. On the basis of material evidence, both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both parties, the tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.3,41,100/- with interest @ 6% p.a. and fixed the liability jointly against respondent Nos.1 and 2 and directed to deposit the compensation amount within 90 days.
3.5. Being aggrieved by the meagre compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimant is before this Court seeking compensation.

4. The main contention of the learned counsel for appellant - claimant is that, the tribunal has committed an error in awarding meagre compensation, which calls for interference at the hands of this Court.
Accordingly, he seeks enhancement of compensation.
Per contra, learned counsel for respondent- Insurance Company submits that the tribunal has rightly awarded just and reasonable compensation, which does not call for interference.

Therefore,
on these grounds, he seeks to dismiss the appeal.
6. Having heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for the respondent - Insurance Company, perused the impugned judgment and award.
On careful perusal of Exs.P1 to P5 are the police records depicts the filing of FIR and Charge sheet laid against the driver of the Car.
Therefore, negligence rightly attributed against the driver of the Car.
Exs. P6
to P20, the medical records, bills, prescriptions to show the injuries suffered and the disability incurred by the claimant.
7. Now coming to the aspect of age, avocation, income, disability and appropriate multiplier for awarding compensation.
It is seen that the claimant was aged 33 years as on the date of occurrence of the accident and the claimant is a driver by profession.
He has produced Ex.P10-Driving License to show that he is a driver by profession, driving a Cab NC: 2024:KHC:14599 vehicle and not using the vehicle for himself.

Therefore, the income of Rs.9,000/- assessed by the tribunal is on the lower side, and he cannot be equated with that of a Coolie or an agriculturist who fall within the bracket of the Notional Income Chart of the Legal Services Authority when he has proved and established that he is a driver by profession.
Therefore, something more will have to be taken than the Notional Income of Rs.12,500/-.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that additional Rs.1,000/- to be added.
Therefore, income has taken as Rs.13,500/- p.m, accepting the argument of learned counsel for the appellant.
8. Doctor has been examined as PW.3, who has opined the disability to an extent of 36% to the left upper limb and whole body disability at 18%.
The tribunal has not satisfied with the opinion expressed by the Doctor-PW.3, has assessed the disability at 6%.

I do not find any good reason for the tribunal to have reduced the disability to such large extent and no cogent reasons are forthcoming by the tribunal for reducing the disability from 18% to 6% as a functional disability.

sentences.text: the tribunal is not an expert in the field of medicine and more so when the Doctor has expressed disability to a particular limb NC: 2024:KHC:14599 and the whole body, maximum the tribunal could do is only assessing functional disability taking into consideration age and avocation of the claimant.
The functional disability in the present case could be taken as 15% as against 6% assessed by the tribunal.

Therefore, the loss of future income due to disability would be Rs.3,88,800/-
(Rs.13,500/- x 12 x 16 x 15%) as against Rs.1,03,680/-.
9. Towards pain and suffering, the tribunal awarded Rs.20,000/-.
This Court deems it appropriate to award Rs.50,000/- under this head, considering the magnitude of injuries suffered by the claimant.
10. Towards medical expenses, the tribunal awarded Rs.1,87,408/-.
Same is retained.
11. Towards food, nourishment and attendant charges, tribunal awarded Rs.15,000/-.
Same is retained.
12. Towards loss of amenities/unhappiness, the tribunal awarded Rs.15,000/-.
This Court deems it appropriate to award Rs.30,000/- under this head.
Towards loss of income during laid up period, the tribunal has not awarded any amount.
The claimant would require at-least three months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day activities.
Therefore, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.40,500/-(Rs.13,500 x 3) under this head.
14. Towards future medical expenses tribunal has not awarded any amount.
PW.3 - Doctor has opined Rs.30,000/- requirement for removal of implants.
This Court deems it appropriate to award Rs.20,000/- under this head.
15. In view of the above discussions, the claimant would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.7,31,708/- as against Rs.3,41,100/- as mentioned in the table below:
